values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' G. Richard Thompson WMA: 11 designated parking areas; Thompson Lake has handicapped parking and a small unimproved boat launch.

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Thompson WMA page that primitive camping is still allowed (listed among the WMA's recreational opportunities; no designated campsites), and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization. Not stated: season, posted hours, which parking areas allow camping. ownership wma stands. Note (with the $10 / $4 Access Permit line) left as is.
flags: 300-ft rule lead: DWR's statewide rule (https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/) says 'It is unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility (building, boat ramp, etc.)'. The entry is named 'Thompson Lake Parking Area', and DWR's WMA map (https://dwr.virginia.gov/wp-content/uploads/media/Thompson-WMA-Map.pdf) shows the parking lot by the kiosk off Route 688 only roughly 150 m east of the lake, beside the lake's boat-ramp and handicapped lot. AWH's note says 'not on the lake'; whether the pinned spot (38.9574,-77.9888) is more than 300 ft from both the lake and the boat ramp needs an imagery check. If it is within 300 ft, camping there is unlawful and the pin should move to another of the 11 parking areas (or the entry drop).
Info: Thompson Lake trout stocking is discontinued indefinitely 'due to inconsistent water levels' (https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/thompson/).
